READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

  1. The subject of false teachers returns (cf. 1 Tim. 1:3-11,19-20; 4:1-5; 6:3-11,17-19). This entire letter addresses the problems caused by the doctrinal and moral issues raised by the heretics.

  2. Verses 1-2 seem out of place, but they probably also relate to the false teachers' messages about Christian slaves and their new rights and freedoms. The UBS4 and TEV both see the structure of this section of the book as Paul encouraging Timothy on how to deal with different groups within the church.
    1. older men and women (1 Tim. 5:1-2)
    2. widows (1 Tim. 5:3-11)
    3. elders (1 Tim. 5:17-25)
    4. slaves (1 Tim. 6:1-2)

  3. Surprisingly, 1 Timothy does not end with a series of personal greetings. Paul stayed longer in Ephesus than in any other city and had tremendous evangelistic results (see Acts 19). He knew many faithful believers in this city. Why greet only Timothy?
     This letter is obviously meant to be read to the assembled church or in the house churches ("you" is PLURAL in 1 Tim. 6:21). However, it was also
    1. a personal letter with advice and instructions specifically for Timothy, his Apostolic surrogate
    2. a letter of recommendation passing on Paul's Apostolic authority to Timothy as his personal representative

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: 1 Timothy 6:2 "Those who have believers as their masters must not be disrespectful to them"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:2 "Those who have believers as their masters must not be disrespectful to them" This is literally "look down,"which is a PRESENT ACTIVE IMPERATIVE with the NEGATIVE PARTICLE, implying stop an act already in process. This phrase relates to the doctrinal concept that everything we as believers do must be of the highest quality for Christ's sake (cf. 1 Cor. 10:31; Eph. 6:6-7; Col. 3:17; 1 Pet. 4:11; also note the NT book of Philemon).

The term "masters" is not the normal term for slave owner, kurios (cf. Eph. 6:5,9; Col. 3:22; 4:1), but despotēs. It is usually used of God the Father and the Son, but in the Pastoral Letters it is used regularly for earthly slave masters (cf. 1 Tim. 6:1,2; 2 Tim. 2:21; Titus 2:9). Paul may have used a different scribe.

▣ "Teach and preach these principles" These are two PRESENT ACTIVE IMPERATIVES, which implies a continual obligation (cf. 1 Tim. 4:11). This phrase can conclude the previous admonition (cf. NASB, NKJV) or introduce what follows (cf. NRSV, TEV, NJB). Remember, chapter and verse divisions are not inspired.

entries.title: 1 Timothy 6:3 "If"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:3 "If" This is a FIRST CLASS CONDITIONAL SENTENCE (which is assumed to be true) continuing the literary context from 1 Tim. 6:3 through 1 Tim. 6:5. There were false teachers who rejected Paul's teachings (cf. 1 Tim. 1:3-7; 4:1-3). They were in the churches (cf. 1 John 2:18-19).

▣ "advocates a different doctrine" This is the Greek term heteros, which means "another of a different kind." The false teaching was a combination of Jewish legalism and Greek philosophy similar to that found in Colossians and Ephesians.

▣ "and does not agree with sound words" See note at 1 Tim. 1:10.

▣ "those of our Lord Jesus Christ" Paul asserts that the origin of the "sound words" is Christ's teachings which were given to Paul. These false teachers rejected both Christ and His Apostles' teachings.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHRIST JESUS AS LORD

▣ "and with doctrine conforming to godliness" See note at 1 Tim. 2:2. Christ's teachings always had godliness as their goal (cf. 1 Tim. 3:16). These false teachers tried to separate truth from life, justification from sanctification, the INDICATIVE (gospel truth) from the IMPERATIVE (gospel godliness). Eternal life has observable characteristics (cf. Matt. 7:15-23).

SPECIAL TOPIC: GODLINESS

SPECIAL TOPIC: NEW TESTAMENT HOLINESS/SANCTIFICATION

6:4
NASB, NRSV  "he is conceited"
NKJV, NJB, Peshitta  "he is proud"
TEV  "is swollen with pride"

This is a PERFECT PASSIVE INDICATIVE. The term is literally "smoke-blinded" by means of pride (cf. 1 Tim. 3:6; 6:4; 2 Tim. 3:4). This is not ignorance but self-willed blindness.

SPECIAL TOPIC: VICES AND VIRTUES IN THE NT

▣ "but he has a morbid interest in controversial questions and disputes about words" There has been an ongoing emphasis on Timothy not being involved in these futile discussions of the false teachers (cf. 1 Tim. 1:3,4; 4:7; 2 Tim. 2:14; 4:4; Titus 1:14). I wonder how this would apply today?

The term "morbid" is literally "to be sick." It came to be used as imagery for an intense craving for something. These false teachers were not seeking godliness, but wanting esoteric knowledge about unrevealed areas or peripheral areas of truth. They wanted to argue over oblique doctrinal issues which only caused arguments and prideful divisions.

The older I get the more I know I do not know and the happier I am with less understanding! The main truths of Christianity are clear and repeated! Yet, somehow we strive to know "all" the details and implications and weave theological webs containing all the inferences of difficult, oblique, apocalyptic and prophetic passages. We glory in our detailed systems instead of our relationship with Christ. It may be harder for a dogmatic, systematic theologian to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich person!!

Preach the clear truths! Discuss the peripherals in love! Be gracious to all! Maturity will make us less judgmental and more Christlike.

entries.title: 1 Timothy 6:5 "men of depraved mind"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:5 "men of depraved mind" This refers to either

  1. the entire context refers to the false teachers
  2. the first few verses refer to them and the rest refers to the consequences caused in the local house churches by their teachings (cf. Arichea and Hatton's A Handbook on Paul's Letters to Timothy and Titus, UBS)

I think the young widows, and also possibly some slaves (cf. 1 Tim. 6:1-2), were surrogate speakers for the false teachers (cf. Gordon Fee's First and Second Timothy and Titus in the New International Biblical Commentary Vol. 13).

▣ "deprived of the truth" Both of these last phrases are PERFECT PASSIVE PARTICIPLES, implying a settled state of mind and heart brought about by an outside agent, probably the evil one. He is the father not only of lies, but also of religious speculation and theological elitism.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SATAN

SPECIAL TOPIC: TRUTH IN JOHN'S WRITINGS

SPECIAL TOPIC: TRUTH IN PAUL'S WRITINGS

▣
NASB  "who suppose that godliness is a means of gain"
NKJV  "who suppose that godliness is a means of gain"
NRSV  "imagining that godliness is a means of gain"
TEV  "They think that religion is a way to become rich"
NJB  "imagine that religion is a way of making a profit"
Peshitta  "who think worshipping God is for worldly gain"

This seems to involve one of two things:

  1. The false teachers taught a theology of success, privilege, and possessions.
  2. They charged for their teaching (cf. Titus 1:11; 2 Pet. 2:3).
  3. Number 2 is probably more likely.

The King James Version adds a phrase at the end of 1 Tim. 6:5, "from such withdraw thyself," but this only occurs in the Corrector of the fifth century Greek uncial manuscript D. It does not occur in the more ancient uncial manuscripts א, A, D*, F, or G. The UBS4 gives the shorter text an "A" rating (certain).

For "godliness" see SPECIAL TOPIC: GODLINESS

entries.title: 1 Timothy 6:6 "when accompanied by contentment"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 6:6 "when accompanied by contentment" This word basically involves not prideful self-sufficiency, but the Holy Spirit-encouraged sufficiency that comes not from circumstance or personal resources, but dependence on God in Christ (cf. Phil. 4:11-13).

entries.title: 1 Timothy 6:7 "For we have brought nothing into the world"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:7 "For we have brought nothing into the world" This may be an allusion to several OT passages (cf. Job 1:21; Ps. 49:17; Eccl. 5:15). It gives a rationale for the statement in 1 Tim. 6:6. Verses 6 and 8 are similar to statements found in the Greek Stoic philosophers. Paul was familiar with these moralists. Many of his lists of sins and virtues are also similar to these Greek writers.

Textual options:

  1. The KJV adds "and it is certain" for "because" of "for." This addition appears in MSS אi2 and D2, as well as some Old Latin, Vulgate, and Syrian versions.
  2. MS D and some Old Latin, Vulgate, and Syriac versions have "true" before "because."
  3. The UBS4 gives the shorter text an "A" rating (certain).

SPECIAL TOPIC: KOSMOS

SPECIAL TOPIC: TEXTUAL CRITICISM

entries.title: 1 Timothy 6:8
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:8 Believers need to be content with God's provision of daily needs (cf. Prov. 30:8; Matt. 6:11). Paul's use of the word "gain" in 1 Tim. 6:5 caused him to elaborate on the false teachers' greed (cf. 1 Tim. 6:6-10 and 17-19).

SPECIAL TOPIC: WEALTH

entries.title: 1 Timothy 6:9 "But those who want to get rich fall into temptation"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:9 "But those who want to get rich fall into temptation" Believers bring many things on themselves because of greed for earthly things, power, and popularity (cf. Prov. 23:4; 28:20; Matt. 6:19-34).

"Temptation" is the Greek term peirasmos, which means "to test with a view toward destruction."

SPECIAL TOPIC: WEALTH

SPECIAL TOPIC: GREEK TERMS FOR TESTING AND THEIR CONNOTATIONS

▣ "and a snare" There are three textual variants.

  1. snare – MSS א, A, D2, H
  2. snares – minuscules 33, 1175, and the Peshitta and Coptic versions
  3. snare of the devil – MSS D*, F, G, and the Old Latin version

The UBS4 gives option #1 an "A" rating (certain).

▣ "ruin and destruction" This concept is used several times in the NT (cf. Matt. 7:13; Rom. 9:22; Phil. 1:28; 3:19; 2 Thess. 2:3; 2 Pet. 2:1; 3:7; Rev. 17:8-11). It is imagery for the violent ceasing of physical life. This term does not relate to the theological concept of annihilation (see Edward Fudge, The Fire That Consumes for a cogent argument for the annihilation of the unbelieving wicked; also a YouTube video  YouTube One Hour Lecture), which asserts that the spiritually lost do not suffer permanent separation, but at some point in time the loss of existence (i.e., limited immortality). Annihilationalists would interpret this literally. This is asserted to be more "humane" of God than an eternal hell. However, the same term (aiōnion) that describes an eternal heaven in Matt. 25:46 is also used to describe an eternal hell. I have benefitted from watching a YouTube video by Steve Gregg called, "Hell—Three Christian Views."  YouTube Lecture - 1:34:57

SPECIAL TOPIC: ETERNAL

entries.title: 1 Timothy 6:10 "For the love of money is a root of all sorts of evil"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:10 "For the love of money is a root of all sorts of evil" This may have been a well-known proverb. Money is not the problem; it is the "love" of money that is the problem! The Greek does not have the DEFINITE ARTICLE with "root" which means it is one of many problems (cf. 2 Tim. 2:25-26; 3:2-5,7-9). Money is a tool, not a goal. It can become a god (mammon, cf. Matt. 6:24; Luke 16:9-13).

The NASB translation, like the NKJV and NRSV, tries to soften the Greek (lit. "for a root of all evils") hyperbole by adding "sorts" (NKJV, NRSV, "kinds of"). Money is not the only temptation (cf. Col. 3:5), but it is a significant one (cf. 1 Tim. 3:3).

SPECIAL TOPIC: WEALTH

▣ "some by longing for it have wandered away from the faith" Does "faith" here speak of salvation or godly living? In this context the false teachers have left the faith and are trying to influence others (cf. Mark 13:22). Greed and financial exploitation (along with sexual exploitation, as well as claiming special knowledge or insight) is a recurrent characteristic of false teachers. If money becomes ultimate, it becomes a god. "Mammon" in Matt. 6:24 is capitalized in NASB because it is assumed to reflect the title of a money god from Syria. Love of money can become idolatrous. It can cause disastrous results in this life and in the next (cf. 1 Tim. 4:1; 5:8; 2 Tim. 2:25-26; Titus 1:16).

It is hard to discern the difference between a lost false teacher and a duped believer. Often they look, think, and act alike. Only God knows the heart. He will make the final decision. Jesus' words in Matthew 7 ("by their fruits you shall know them") and Matthew 13 (the parable of the soils) are very troubling to our cherished systematic theologies.

SPECIAL TOPIC: APOSTASY (APHISTĒMI)

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FAITH

SPECIAL TOPIC: PERSEVERANCE

entries.title: 1 Timothy 6:11 "But flee from these things"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:11 "But flee from these things" Timothy is commanded (PRESENT ACTIVE IMPERATIVE, cf. 2 Tim. 2:22) to flee from the things discussed in 1 Tim. 6:3-10 (i.e., endless controversies and/or love of money). This is in contrast to the things he was to preach and teach (cf. 1 Tim. 6:2b), which are listed in 1 Tim. 5:1-6:2a. Christianity involves initial and continuing choices!

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

▣
NASB. NRSV, TEV  "you man of God"
NKJV, Peshitta  "O man of God"
NJB  "as someone dedicated to God"

This was an honorific title from the OT which was used of Moses (i.e., Deut. 33:1; Josh. 14:6), Elijah, Elisha, Samuel, David, and unnamed prophets (i.e., 1 Sam. 2:27; 1 Kgs. 12:22; 13:1). In 2 Tim. 3:16,17 it is used for all believers equipped by the word of God. The false teachers are not men of God nor are they equipped by the Word of God.

▣ "pursue" This is another PRESENT ACTIVE IMPERATIVE, an ongoing command. The first ("flee") is negative, the second, IMPERATIVE ("pursue") is positive. Both are crucial for sound teaching and personal righteousness.

▣ "righteousness" This must refer to holy living (cf. James 3:13-18), not to imputed (forensic) righteousness as in Romans 4. Romans 1-8 (a doctrinal summary) speaks of our position in Christ (i.e., justification). The Pastoral Letters (letters against false teaching) speak of our possessing our possession (i.e., sanctification).

This list of Christlike qualities is exactly opposite of the lifestyles of the false teachers. By their fruits you shall know them (cf. Matth. 7:15-23).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SANCTIFICATION

SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS

▣ "godliness" This is a recurring theme (cf. 1 Tim. 3:10; 4:7-8; 6:3,5-6; 2 Tim. 3:5). Eternal life has observable characteristics. To know God is to be (desire to be) like God (cf. Matt. 5:48).

SPECIAL TOPIC: GODLINESS

▣
NASB, NJB  "perseverance"
NKJV, Peshitta  "patience"
NRSV, TEV  "endurance"

The Greek word hupomonē has several possible English translations. In A Greek-English Lexicon of the New Testament, Bauer, Arndt, Gingrich, and Danker say that this word refers to the enduring of toil and suffering (p. 846). Timothy was to face

  1. the problems
  2. those who caused the problems
  3. those affected by the problems with a steadfast endurance

SPECIAL TOPIC: PERSEVERANCE

▣ "gentleness" Not only was Timothy to endure and persevere, but he was to do so with a faithful, loving, gentle spirit (cf. 1 Tim. 3:3; 2 Tim. 2:25; Titus 3:3; Gal. 6:1; James 1:21; 3:13,17; 1 Pet. 2:18; 3:4).

entries.title: 1 Timothy 6:12 "Fight the good fight of faith"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:12 "Fight the good fight of faith" This is a PRESENT MIDDLE (deponent) IMPERATIVE. The cognate VERB and NOUN are used here to intensify the athletic (cf. 1 Tim. 1:18; Heb. 12:1-3) or military (cf. Eph. 6:10-18) imagery (Paul also "fought the good fight," cf. 2 Tim. 4:7). We get the English word "agony" from this imagery.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FAITH

▣ "take hold of the eternal life" This is an AORIST MIDDLE IMPERATIVE (cf. 1 Tim. 6:19). This is imagery for the winning athlete receiving the trophy or crown. This shows mankind's need to initially respond (cf. 1 Tim. 6:12b) and continue to respond in faith. The next phrase shows God's keeping power (cf. 1 Tim. 6:12c). These are both true and valid covenantal aspects of salvation; they are paradoxical, but true (cf. Phil. 2:12-13)! Eternal life is a way of referring to the consummation of the gospel hope (i.e. glorification, cf. Rom. 8:30; see SPECIAL TOPIC: HOPE). See full note at 2 Tim. 1:10.

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

▣ "to which you were called" This emphasis on God's electing and keeping power (cf. 1 Cor. 1:9) must be combined with our daily faith cooperation. Predestination and perseverance must be held together as two sides of one coin.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CALLED

SPECIAL TOPIC: ELECTION/PREDESTINATION AND THE NEED FOR A THEOLOGICAL BALANCE

▣ "and you made the good confession" This is the Greek word homologeō, which speaks of a public profession or confession (cf. 1 John 1:9). In this context it seems to refer to Timothy's baptism as his public profession of faith. Early believers may have repeated the formula "Jesus is Lord" (cf. Rom. 10:9-13) as their personal and public profession of faith in Jesus. This brief phrase implied His humanity, Deity, atonement, and exaltation (cf. Phil. 2:6-11).

SPECIAL TOPIC: CONFESSION/PROFESSION

SPECIAL TOPIC: BAPTISM

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHRIST JESUS AS LORD

▣ "in the presence of many witnesses" This may refer to

  1. Timothy's ordination (cf. 1 Tim. 5:14; 2 Tim. 1:6)
  2. his public profession before the local church (cf. Acts 16:1-2)
  3. more probably, his baptism

entries.title: 1 Timothy 6:13 "I charge you in the presence of God"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:13 "I charge you in the presence of God" Verses 13-16 are one sentence in Greek. As Timothy confessed Jesus publicly (cf. Matt. 10:32-33), now Paul charges him also in God's presence (cf. 1 Tim. 5:21; 2 Tim. 4:1).

Paul "charges" or commands Timothy often in the Pastoral Letters. Sometimes these refer to things that Timothy should do (cf. 1 Tim. 1:3,18; 4:11; 5:21; 6:13; 2 Tim. 4:1) and sometimes to what he should tell others (cf. 1 Tim. 5:7,21; 6:17; 2 Tim. 2:14).

The PRONOUN "you" is in the INFINITIVE "to keep" of 1 Tim. 6:14. Some MSS inserted it after the VERB "I charge" in 1 Tim. 6:13 (MSS אi2, A, D, H). It is omitted in MSS א*, F, G. UBS4 cannot decide which is original. Obviously, like so many Greek variants, it does not affect the meaning of the long sentence from verse 13 to verse 16.

▣
NASB, NKJV, REB, TEV, NRSV, NET  "gives life"
Peshitta  "the giver of life"
NJB  "the source of all life"

This is literally "bring forth life (PRESENT ACTIVE PARTICIPLE) to all things." God is the origin and source of all life (cf. 1 Tim. 1:17; 6:16; 2 Tim. 1:10). There is no life apart from Him. The OT title YHWH, from the Hebrew VERB "to be" (cf. Exod. 3:14), is a word play on this very concept. God is the only one who can give and sustain physical and eternal life.

This term has connotations of both

  1. giving life (cf. 1 Sam. 2:6; 1 Tim. 6:13)
  2. preserving life (cf. Jdgs. 8:19; 1 Sam. 27:9,11; 1 Kgs. 21:31; Luke 17:33; Acts 7:19)

YHWH does both through Christ.

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN, C. and D.

▣ "and of Christ Jesus, who testified the good confession before Pontius Pilate" Jesus is called the "Faithful witness" (cf. Rev. 1:5; 3:14). The term "before" (enōpion) can mean

  1. "front of"
  2. "in the time of"

Therefore, this could refer to Jesus' entire life of witness or specifically His trials (cf. Matt. 27:2; John 18:33-37).

SPECIAL TOPIC: PONTIUS PILATE

entries.title: 1 Timothy 6:14 "that you keep the commandment without stain or reproach"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:14 "that you keep the commandment without stain or reproach" This may refer to 1 Tim. 6:11 and 12. Timothy was to live in obedience and purity, unlike the false teachers.

SPECIAL TOPIC: GODLINESS

SPECIAL TOPIC: BLAMELESS, INNOCENT, GUILTLESS, WITHOUT REPROACH

▣ "until the appearing of" In 2 Tim. 1:10 and Titus 2:11 this term (epiphaneia) is used of Jesus' first coming, but here and in 2 Thess. 2:8; 2 Tim. 4:1,8; Titus 2:13 it is used of His Second Coming. The Second Coming has always been a strong incentive to live the Christian life.

SPECIAL TOPIC: NT TERMS FOR CHRIST'S RETURN

entries.title: 1 Timothy 6:15 "which He will bring about at the proper time"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:15 "which He will bring about at the proper time" This same phrase is used in 1 Tim. 2:6 and Titus 1:3 of Jesus' first coming. The "He" describes God the Father's knowledge and control over the first and second comings of the Messiah (cf. Matt. 24:36; Acts 1:7). The Jerome Biblical Commentary (p. 357) suggests that 1 Tim. 6:15-16 are a quote from a Christian hymn (like 1 Tim. 1:17; 3:16; 2 Tim. 2:11-13).

▣ "He who is the blessed and only Sovereign, the King of kings and Lord of lords" This prayer is similar to 1 Tim. 1:17. These descriptive phrases initially and contextually refer to God the Father:

  1. "blessed" (1 Tim. 1:1)
  2. "only Sovereign" (1 Tim. 1:17; cf. Ecclesiasticus 46:5)
  3. "Lord of lords" (Deut. 10:17; Ps. 136:3)

The title "King of kings" is parallel to "Lord of lords" and is used of Jesus in Rev. 17:14; 19:16. It originally referred to the kings of Mesopotamia, but was used by the Jews during the interbiblical period to refer to YHWH.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (NT)

entries.title: 1 Timothy 6:16 "who alone possesses immortality"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:16 "who alone possesses immortality" This is the term "death" with the ALPHA PRIVATIVE (cf. 1 Cor. 15:53-54). This seems to be the basic meaning of the OT title "YHWH," the ever-living, only-living One (cf. Exod. 3:14-16). Notice the inference of monotheism (i.e., "who alone possesses")! YHWH is the origin and source of life and there is no other! There is no life apart from Him. See F. F. Bruce, Answers to Questions, p. 215.

The ancient Greek philosophers (esp. Plato) assert the pre-existence and post existence immortality of the spiritual aspect of humans known as the "soul." However, this verse clearly expresses the biblical truth that only YHWH is "eternal." Only He has immortality.

The mortality of Adam and Eve, after they violated YHWH's command, is seen by their being removed from the Tree of Life. Eternal life is a gift from God, given to believers in Jesus Christ (i.e., 1 Cor. 15:53,54; 2 Cor. 5:4). The early church fathers, especially Augustine, were affected by the Platonic presupposition.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM

▣ "and dwells in unapproachable light" The rabbis called the "cloud of glory" the Shekinah, which is from the Hebrew term "to dwell" (with the implication "to dwell with permanently," cf. Exod. 24:17; 23:20; see notes online).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SHEKINAH

▣ "whom no man has seen or can see" In the OT God's holiness was so awesome that no sinful human could see God and live (cf. Gen. 16:13; 32:30; Exod. 20:19; 33:18-20; Jdgs. 6:22-23; 13:22; Isa. 6:5; John 6:46; 1 John 4:12). In the NT believers have seen Him truly revealed in Jesus (cf. John 1:18; 6:46; 14:8-9) and will see Him personally one day (cf. Matt. 5:8; Heb. 12:14; Rev. 22:40).

SPECIAL TOPIC: CAN HUMANS SEE GOD AND LIVE?

▣ "to Him be honor and eternal dominion" Paul often breaks into a doxology of praise to God the Father (cf. 1 Tim. 1:17; Eph. 3:20-21). The Son is the Father's instrument of creation, revelation, redemption, and judgment. However, the eternal kingdom belongs to the Father through the Son (cf. Dan. 7:13; 1 Cor. 15:25-28).

▣ "Amen" This is a Hebrew idiom of affirmation.

SPECIAL TOPIC: AMEN

entries.title: 1 Timothy 6:17 "Instruct those who are rich in this present world not to be conceited"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:17 "Instruct those who are rich in this present world not to be conceited" As verse 9 warns about an evil desire for money, verse 17 warns those who have money against putting their faith in it and not in Christ (cf. Matt. 6:19-21; 13:22; 19:23-30; James 1:9-11; 5:1-6).

For "this present world" see SPECIAL TOPIC: THIS AGE AND THE AGE TO COME

▣ "or to fix their hope on the uncertainty of riches" This is a PERFECT ACTIVE INFINITIVE. Humans tend to trust in their resources, not God's resources (cf. 1 Tim. 4:10; 5:5). Some of Jesus' strongest words were directed at the wealthy (cf. Luke 18:18-30).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HOPE

SPECIAL TOPIC: WEALTH

▣ "but on God" There are several variants.

  1. on God – א, F, G
  2. on (the) God – MSS A, I, P
  3. on God living – MS D*
  4. on (the) God (the) living – MS D2

The UBS4 gives option #1 an "A" rating. The descriptive form is taken from 1 Tim. 4:10.

SPECIAL TOPIC: TEXTUAL CRITICISM

entries.title: 1 Timothy 6:17-19
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 6:17-19 One wonders if 1 Tim. 6:17-19 were an after thought or if Paul received more information about the house churches in Ephesus. It is also possible that Paul wrote 1 Tim. 6:17-21 himself, as he regularly closed his letters with his own handwriting (cf. 2 Thess. 3:17-18).

entries.title: 1 Timothy 6:18 "Instruct them"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:18 "Instruct them" Here are Paul's threefold guidelines for those who have worldly goods.

  1. continue doing good (cf. 1 Tim. 5:10; 2 Tim. 2:21; 3:17; Titus 3:1,8,14)
  2. be ready to share
  3. be generous (cf. 2 Corinthians 8-9)

entries.title: 1 Timothy 6:19
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:19 This verse reminds one of Jesus' Sermon on the Mount, especially chapter 6 (cf. Luke 12:15). It uses two examples:

  1. storing up true riches
  2. building a sure and strong foundation (i.e., Matt. 7:24-27)

The wise use of wealth does both! By them believers take hold of true life (i.e., eternal life, cf. 1 Tim. 6:12).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SERMON ON THE MOUNT

▣
NASB  "life indeed"
NKJV  "eternal life"
NRSV  "the life that really is life"
TEV  "the life which is true life"
NJB  "the only life that is real"
Peshitta  "the true life"

The variety of the English translations involves the choice of

  1. ontōs – MSS א, A, D*, F, G (NASB)
  2. aiōniou – MS D2 (NKJV)
  3. both – minuscules 69, 296, 467, and 1175 (these copyists must have had Greek manuscripts that had both options)

The UBS4 gives option #1 and "A" rating.

SPECIAL TOPIC: TEXTUAL CRITICISM

entries.title: 1 Timothy 6:20 "guard what has been entrusted to you"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:20 "guard what has been entrusted to you" The VERB is an AORIST ACTIVE IMPERATIVE. The term "entrusted" is related to the banking term for "deposit," which is used three times in the Pastoral Letters for "the gospel" (cf. 1 Tim. 1:11, see full note at 1 Tim. 1:18) or the body of Christian truth (cf. Acts 6:7; 13:8; 14:22; Gal. 1:23; 3:23; 6:10; Phil. 1:27; Jude 1:3,20). Believers are stewards of the gospel (cf. 1 Cor. 4:1-2; 2 Tim. 1:12,14).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE KERYGMA OF THE EARLY CHURCH

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE ORTHODOXY OF THE PASTORALS

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE GOSPEL

▣ "avoiding worldly and empty chatter and the opposing arguments of what is falsely called knowledge" "Avoiding" is a PRESENT MIDDLE PARTICIPLE used as an IMPERATIVE. 1 Timothy is a letter primarily about heresy, not church organization. The guidelines in the book are directly related to the problems caused by the false teachers, not necessarily universal guidelines for all churches of all times in all places.

▣ "knowledge" The false teachers in the Pastoral Letters are a combination of "Jewish legalists" and Greek Gnostics (much like those in Colossians and Ephesians). "Knowledge," usually secret or specially revealed knowledge, was the claim of these teachers. These false teachers separated truth from life, justification from sanctification, and turned salvation into a secret, special knowledge divorced from godliness.

SPECIAL TOPIC: GNOSTICISM

6:21
NASB  "which some have professed and thus gone astray from the faith"
NKJV, Peshitta  "by professing it, some have strayed concerning the faith"
NRSV  "by professing it some have missed the mark as regards the faith"
TEV  "for some have claimed to possess it, and as a result
  they have lost the way of faith"
NJB  "by adopting this, some have missed the goal of faith"

This same word is used in 1 Tim. 1:6 to describe the false teachers; also notice 1 Tim. 1:19; 4:1-2; 5:15; 6:10. There are so many strong warnings in this book!

Remember Christianity is

  1. a person to be welcomed
  2. doctrine to be believed
  3. a corresponding life to be lived

If any one of these is de-emphasized or left out, then tremendous problems occur (cf. Matt. 7:21-27).

SPECIAL TOPIC: APOSTASY

▣ "Grace be with you" The "you" is PLURAL (MS D). This shows that the letter, although addressed to an individual (singular "you" in MSS א, A, F, G), was to be read publicly. Notice Paul prays for them God's grace and true knowledge (cf. 1 Tim. 6:20)! This same PLURAL ending is in all the Pastoral Letters (cf. 2 Tim. 4:22; Titus 3:15).

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

  1. Why didn't the Christian church attack the issue of slavery? (Other passages of Paul's which deal with slaves are 1 Cor. 7:21-24; Gal. 3:28; Eph. 6:5-9; Col. 3:22-25; Philemon 1:16,17; Titus 2:9; 1 Pet. 2:18).
  2. What do verses 1 and 2 say about our modern day employer/employee relationships?
  3. What is heresy?
  4. What is the difference between a false teacher and differences in interpretation?
  5. Is money evil?
  6. Describe as much as you can the theology of the false teachers.
